16.text: hair on. For rubbing the skins the Chukchee women use mainly reindeer-

17.text: dung and human urine, and sometimes meat-broth. Other tribes apply oil,

18.text: putrid liver, fish-eggs (fresh, putrid, or dried, and subsequently soaked in water),

19.text: bran, etc. Nevertheless the reindeer-skins of Chukchee make are softer and

20.text: better dyed than those of any of their neighbors. The usual process begins

21.text: with folding a fresh skin with the flesh side in, and leaving it in this state

22.text: over night. If dry, the skin is previously soaked in water. In the morning

23.text: the flesh side of the skin is scraped with the iron scraper and trampled with

24.text: the feet, the right heel being covered with the back part of a short summer

25.text: boot, the toe of which has been cut off at the instep to allow freer motion

26.text: of the foot. The skin is then smeared over with reindeer-dung, and again

27.text: left over night. After that, it is scraped a second time and trampled with

28.text: the heels. A vessel filled with urine and some alder-bark cut fine is warmed

29.text: for an hour over an ordinary lamp. When the liquor is sufficiently saturated,

30.text: the inside of the skin is well rubbed with it, and the skin is hung up in the

31.text: sleeping-room to dry. After drying, it is again gone over with the scraper,

32.text: and all tough places are dampened with urine, scraped, and dyed anew.

33.text: With the largest skins the scraping is repeated several times. Each time

34.text: the skin is left to dry over night. The scraping is begun with the stone

35.text: scraper, and continued with the iron one. The more scrapings the skin has

36.text: undergone, the softer and finer it becomes in the end.

37.text: The dyeing with alder-bark is considered quite indispensable for every

38.text: part of the reindeer-skin, even for the tough strips taken from the legs, which

39.text: are used for boots and mittens. This process makes the skin softer, and

40.text: corresponds somewhat to tanning. The dyed skins will keep off dampness
